committee_action.action: Deliberated upon by the Mother Committee on 2017-03-07
committee_action.meethigh:
The Presiding Officer, Vice Chairperson Dennis Laogan, informed the body that a similar bill was filed and approved on third reading during the 15th and 16th Congresses. He expressed hope that it will be enacted in the 17th Congress.

The representatives from the concerned agencies and public sector unions, namely, the Civil Service Commission (CSC), Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), Cooperative Dev. Authority (CDA), Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP), Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP),  Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Confederation of Independent Unions in the Public Sector (CIU), Public Services Labor Independent Confederation (PSLINK) and Philippine Government Employees Association (PGEA) lauded the intent of the measure and manifested their full support therefor.    

	CSC proposed the inclusion in the bill of a provision to safeguard public interest since it is the agencyâ€™s understanding that the bill covers entrepreneurial activities of government employees while in-service.

Among the other comments and recommendations given were:

(1) DTI:  for the entrepreneurial skills development to be administered two years before retirement; for each agency to have in-house counselors/business tutors for retiring government employees, with the regular fund to be taken from the agency; and for the academe to be tapped in the Coordinating Council on Government Employeesâ€™ Entrepreneurship Development Program that will be created, as provided for in the bill; 

(2) LBP:   instead of creating the Council, for the CSC to spearhead the coordination among the concerned government agencies and the four public sector unions in the preparation, implementation and monitoring of a comprehensive plan for government employeesâ€™ entrepreneurial development;

(3) DBP:  for the inclusion of a provision that the financing of the entrepreneurial projects of government employees shall be dependent on the strength and quality of the proposed enterpriseâ€™s project and business cash flows, overall credit worthiness, and other mitigating measures, subject to due diligence, in order to  ensure the sustainability of funds of Government Financial Institutions (GFIs) which will be set aside for the purpose;

(4) PSLINK: to maintain a database of retirees, including their entrepreneurial engagements,  for accurate information and reference;  for a mandatory conduct of entrepreneurial and related seminar in all government agencies for its officials and employees as part of the agencyâ€™s annual training plan; and harmonization with the Go Negosyo Law; and 

(5) PGEA:  to also give emphasis on the follow-up programs after the retirees have set-up their business.

The representatives from GSIS, CIU and PGEA obliged to submit their official position papers within the week.

The Committee approved to convene a technical working group (TWG), to be chaired by Rep. Laogan, in order to fine-tune the provisions of the bill.  Rep. Laogan requested the agencies to submit the names of their representatives to the TWG.

committee_action.action: Deliberated by the TWG on 2017-05-04
committee_action.meethigh:
There being no objection, said Section 4 now reads as follows:

â€œSection 4. Establishment of Entrepreneurial Training Programs. â€“ All government offices and agencies shall prepare and implement a post-service Government Service Entrepreneurship Development Program (GSEDP) for their employees based on guidelines prescribed by the Civil Service Commission (CSC). The GSEDP shall be designed in such a manner as to help employees learn what they need to know to develop ideas and actualize them into successful businesses and how to increase entrepreneurial opportunities in their respective municipalities, provinces and regions. The GSEDP shall introduce employees to technology transfer systems, entrepreneurial educational programs, entrepreneurial networks, financial literacy and livelihood trainings/seminars, as part of the agencyâ€™s annual training plan.

â€œIntensive preparation activities and learning modules for retirees shall start five (5) years prior to their retirement date. The post-service assistance may be given on a consultancy basis to strengthen the proposed programs to be implemented under this Act.

â€œEach agency shall have full-time, in-house business tutors and counsellors on the implementation of the proposed programs for retiring employees. The regular funding for the program shall be taken from the agencyâ€™s annual budget.â€�

In Section 5, Rep. Noel opted to delete the last portion of Section 5 regarding the preferential rights of government employeesâ€™ cooperatives to operate revenue-generating activities in available government-owned sites and facilities, said Section 5 to now read, as follows:

â€œSection 5.   Establishment of Cooperatives and Savings and Loan Associations. â€“ All government agencies shall promote and support the establishment of cooperatives with the assistance of the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) and of savings and loans associations, by recognizing, protecting and upholding the rights of employees to organize cooperatives and savings and loan associations in their respective offices to generate financial resources and develop employeesâ€™ entrepreneurial skills. Existing cooperatives and savings and loans associations in government agencies shall incorporate the development of employeesâ€™ entrepreneurial skills as part of their objective. Cooperatives and savings and loan associations shall be encouraged to retain the membership of employees even after retirement from public service.â€�

After deliberating on Section 6, the TWG agreed to add a proviso therein, to now read as follows:

â€œSEC. 6. Networking with Government Financial Institutions.  - The heads of all government agencies, including government-owned and controlled corporations concerned, shall coordinate with existing government financial institutions (GFIs) to provide sources of financing for the viable income-generating entrepreneurial projects of their retired employees, subject to the mandate of the GFI concerned. Experts from the GFIs shall be called upon to conduct lectures, workshops in capacity building for entrepreneurship skills and live case studies of successful entrepreneurs. Participants shall be taught to identify and evaluate opportunities for new ventures and to understand how the capital investment process works. All GFIs shall set aside funds for this purpose: Provided, That financing of the entrepreneurial projects of retired government employees shall be dependent on the strength and quality of the proposed enterpriseâ€™s project and business cash flows, overall credit worthiness and other mitigating measures, in accordance with safe and sound banking practices, where applicable.â€�

The TWG likewise  agreed to adopt the recommendation of LBP on Section 7 for the CSC to spearhead the coordination among government agencies for the preparation, implementation and monitoring of a comprehensive plan for the government employees entrepreneurial development, as well as its funding sources, instead of creating a Council as provided for in the bill.  

Furthermore, Rep. Noel enjoined each agency to prepare and submit to the CSC a comprehensive plan to develop entrepreneurial capabilities, managerial expertise and technical skills and also to monitor the implementation of the program.  The CSC was requested to submit the agencyâ€™s confirmation on the afore-stated role of the CSC the following week.

Inputs were also made by the TWG in Sections 7, 8 and 9, which now read, to wit:

â€œSEC. 7. Monitoring of the Government Employeesâ€™Entrepreneurship Development Program. â€“ The Civil Service Commission (CSC) shall spearhead the coordination among all agencies and the four public sector unions in the preparation, implementation and monitoring of a comprehensive plan for the government employeesâ€™ entrepreneurial development, including funding sources.

â€œEach agency shall be tasked to prepare and submit to the CSC a comprehensive plan to develop entrepreneurial capabilities, managerial expertise, financial planning and technical skills, and fund sources.

â€œSEC. 8. Post-service Assistance. â€“ All government agencies shall extend post-service assistance to their respective retirees and shall include this as part of their human resources development plan. They shall develop a post-service assistance program to backstop aspiring entrepreneurs in the development and implementation of their ideas. The program shall cover the entire gamut of the venture creation process from idea generation to building viable business, with emphasis on the nurturing roles of the GFIs, and highlighting successful entrepreneurs as models. The assistance shall include follow-up programs after the business has been set-up, in order to ensure the profitability and sustainability of the business.

â€œSEC. 9. Implementing Rules and Regulations. â€“ The CSC shall promulgate the rules and regulations needed to implement the provisions of this Act within sixty (60) days after it effectivity.â€�
	
	The Secretariat was directed to prepare and finalize the substitute bill reflecting the amendments agreed upon, and the committee report thereon, for the consideration and approval of the Mother Committee.

committee_action.action: Referred to the Technical Working Group (TWG) on 2017-05-18
committee_action.meethigh:
The TWG agreed on the following amendments: 

1.	On Section 2 (Declaration of Policy): Insert the phrase â€œand programsâ€� after the word â€œplansâ€�.

2.	On Section 3 (Objectives):
 a) In paragraph (a), the Secretariat was directed to find another term for    â€œhassle-freeâ€�.  Change â€œpoorest provincesâ€� to â€œpoorest populationsâ€�  where the P3 Program will be made available, as suggested by Rep. Tan;
 b)  In paragraph (b), change the word â€œreplaceâ€� with the phrase â€œprovide a      better alternative toâ€� in referring to informal lenders. 
   
3.	On Section 6 (Features of the P3 Fund):  Instead of specifying the loanable amount and minimal interest rate, the TWG proposed  that â€œThe loanable amount for individual loans, and the interest rate to the conduits and to the end beneficiaries shall be set and regularly reviewed by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development (MSMED) Council: Provided,That the interest rate shall be lower than the prevailing interest rate charged by the micro finance institutions (MFIs)â€�, and that â€œThe interest earnings shall accrue to the P3 Fundâ€�.  

4.	On Section 7 (Policy Oversight Function):  Clarified that the MSMED Council shall perform â€œpolicyâ€� oversight functions on the P3 Fund; and that the MSMED Council shall â€œsubmit to the President and to Congress, through the Congressional Oversight Committee on Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development (COC-MSMED), a yearly report on the status of the P3 Fundâ€�.

	SB Corp. was requested to craft the revised language for the Appropriations Section and submit the same to the Secretariat.
	
	The Secretariat was directed to prepare and e-mail the draft substitute bill reflecting the amendments based on the discussions and agreements arrived at by the TWG.  The TWG participants were requested to review the same and submit their comments thereon the following week.

	Rep. Tan stated that the substitute bill will be presented to the Mother Committee in its meeting scheduled on May 29, 2017, 1:30 P.M. at the Speaker Jose Laurel Hall,  South Wing Annex, House of Representatives, for its consideration and approval.

committee_action.action: Recommendations submitted by the TWG on 2017-05-23
committee_action.remarks: Presentation by the TWG of the Substitute Bill on House Bill No. 3335, introduced by Rep. Victoria Isabel C. Noel, entitled : â€œAn Act Promoting the Development of Entrepreneurship Skills Among Government Employees to Inspire Innovativeness and to Ensure their Productivity Even Beyond Government Serviceâ€�
committee_action.meethigh:
Rep. Victoria Isabel Noel presented the report of the Technical Working Group (TWG) which met on May 4, 2017 to fine-tune the provisions of House Bill 3335.  She discussed the amendments to the bill, based on the discussions and agreements arrived at by the TWG, and the resultant substitute bill.

Mr. Alan Alegria of the Civil Service Commission (CSC)  informed the body that the CSC Chairman confirmed the Commissionâ€™s acceptance of its task pursuant to Section 7 of the bill, that is, to be the lead agency in the preparation, implementation and monitoring of a comprehensive plan for the government employeesâ€™ entrepreneurial development.

Atty. Leilani Capule of the Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP) suggested in Section 6 that the provision by the government financial institutions (GFIs) of sources of financing for the viable projects of retired employees shall be subject, not only to the mandate of the GFI concerned but also to â€œexisting banking laws and regulations, where applicableâ€�.

Director Mary Adelino of the Commission on Audit (COA) submitted its written comments specifically on funding sources.  On motion of Rep. Angelina Tan, Dir. Adelino was requested to reconcile COAâ€™s comments with its previously-submitted one and re-submit its revised comments the following day.

The Committee agreed to defer the approval of the substitute bill until the Committeeâ€™s next meeting on May 29, 2017, pending the submission by the COA of its revised comments.

committee_action.remarks: On motion of Rep. Angelina Tan, duly seconded by Rep. Carlito Marquez, the Committee approved the substitute bill on House Bill 3335, subject to style.  Thereafter, on motion of Rep. Tan, duly seconded by Rep. Acosta, the Committee approved the Committee report on the substitute bill on HB 3335, subject to style.
